findings: ANVIL_STATION_TIMEOUT_SECONDS and runtime.station_timeout_seconds are validated by parse_station_timeout (positive integer only, bool rejected, clamped to the 7200 ceiling) before use. The value goes only into subprocess timeout arithmetic and an env var, never into a shell string or path, so there is no injection sink.

The 7200 ceiling holds on both the environment and anvil.yaml paths, so a runaway station still dies. Fail closed: an invalid value makes the wrapper exit 10, and the executor constructor raises. The wrapper's timeout is the total for the invocation, correction attempt included, so no retry can extend the cap.

The timeout record carries only the station id, timing, the configured timeout, the model and the usage reason. No environment values or secrets are echoed. The only echo of untrusted text is the rejected timeout value in the ValueError message, which is low risk.

The change adds no new endpoint, dependency, outbound call or file-write location, and no permission is broadened. The executor timeout rises to 7200 in anvil.yaml, which is bounded by the ceiling. The change is standard library only.

Minor, non-blocking: a malformed ANVIL_STATION_TIMEOUT_SECONDS in the executor process environment raises an uncaught ValueError from CommandExecutor.__init__ instead of an ExecutorError. This fails closed, with a clear message.
